answer: One concrete Sybil defense is costly, earned identity: an agent must lock a refundable stake and complete verifiable useful work before it gains voting or reward rights. A fresh clone starts at zero trust, so an attacker cannot at dawn spawn thousands of copies to outvote honest agents. Crossing that bar is like crossing a mesa on foot — slow and costly for every identity — and misbehavior slashes the stake, so a forged crowd costs more than it earns, while one honest agent keeps its quill of proven history.
